title: Security configuration bypass through the unauthenticated admin config endpoint
summary: Security controls for every later invoice are removed or weakened until the configuration is reset. Fraudulent invoices are approved more easily. The same endpoint also accepts custom_goals.

LC.rationale: The unauthenticated admin config endpoint accepts attacker-supplied natural-language custom_goals and threshold values that are written to the FinBotConfig row and injected into the system prompt of every later run, reaching the privileged approve_invoice tool path without mediation.

CP.rationale: The custom_goals text and weakened thresholds persist in the FinBotConfig database row and are injected into the system prompt of every later run, remaining reachable after the originating session ends.

AP.rationale: The effect is confined to the single FinBot agent and its own configuration; there are no handoffs and no other agent, tenant, or policy domain is crossed.

RH.rationale: The agent can reach the approve_invoice tool and the CTF flag-awarding logic that acts as a reward channel on the path, but no human-verified reward-hacking episode is documented in the packet.

ES.rationale: Five fixed tools are defined in code with no dynamic tools, MCP servers, plugins, or skills, and the binding is fixed and allowlisted outside model output.

agentic_applicability.rationale: The lab models FinBot as an autonomous invoice processing assistant that uses OpenAI function calling to select and sequence tools across up to five iterations.
